title: Integral derived reduction detects isomorphisms
statement: For ℓ and finite normed E/ℚ_ℓ, use the coefficient rings and scalar functors of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. Let X be any scheme with noetherian underlying space and M,N bounded constructible complexes of internal O_E coefficient modules. If derived reduction of a morphism φ:M→N along O_E→O_E/(ℓ) is invertible in the full residue derived category, then φ is invertible. No properness or exchange assumption is made.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), integral constructibility and derived Nakayama

proof.text: Identify finite presentations of the pulled continuous integral coefficient ring with the integral constructible sheaves of Proposition 6.8.11(3), using the coefficient realization on pro-etale neighborhoods. Establish closure under kernels, cokernels and extensions for these particular integral coefficients: noetherianity of the scheme is not by itself sufficient. The stratified finite presentation description and the DVR structure imply these coefficient-dependent closure assertions.
The cone C of φ is bounded constructible by the weak Serre class criterion. Derived tensor reduction takes it to the cone of the reduced morphism, which is zero.

On each stratum, top-degree right exactness of derived tensor identifies H^b(C⊗^L A) with H^b(C)⊗ A whenever C has no cohomology above b. This zero reduction forces the locally finite O_E-module H^b(C) to be zero, since ℓ belongs to the maximal ideal and Nakayama applies. Repeat through the finite interval of possible cohomology. All cohomology vanishes, so C=0 and φ is an isomorphism.
